newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia says no decision to freeze Singapore ties.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia says no decision to freeze Singapore ties.

text.p: The Malaysian government said on Thursday it had not made any decision to freeze ties with Singapore.
"No decison has been made to freeze ties with Singapore as reported by the local newspapers," a statement issued by acting Foreign Minister Abang Abu Bakar Abang Mustapha said.

On Wednesday cabinet ministers told the national news agency Bernama that all fresh dealings would be suspended following a row triggered by a remark from Singapore Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew about the south Malaysian state of Johor.

The Malaysian cabinet had discussed Malaysian-Singapore ties, the statement said. "I would like to stress that whatever has been reported by the mass media as their main subject in the leading local newspapers today are not accurate," it said.

"What is meant is that the government is studying the implications of the episode towards two-way relations with Singapore following the statement by Singapore Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew on Johor and the reaction of the Singapore government toward the statement," it added.

Lee sparked the row after saying in a court affidavit that Johor was "notorious for shootings, muggings and car-jackings". Lee apologised for the remarks and has ordered his attorney to retract them from an affidavit Lee filed in a libel suit against a Singaporean opposition politician.
